facts.state_of_play: Explosions reported in Kyiv after Zelenskyy warned of a Russian massive attack planned over several days; Russia has now struck Ukrainian cities with missiles, drones, and glide bombs, killing at least 10 civilians. North Korean ballistic missiles were used in strikes on Zaporizhzhia, killing seven civilian workers at the Metinvest steel plant and injuring 21; three more civilians including a 15-year-old boy were killed by Russian drones and artillery. Zelenskyy also warns Putin will use the Russian election — in which opposition to the war is banned — as a pretext for a major troop call-up. Russia's Supreme Court has now banned the country's only anti-war party from next month's parliamentary elections, the latest move to silence dissent. Ukraine is also targeting Wildberries, a Russian retail giant akin to Amazon, as part of an effort to bring the sense of war home to the Russian population. The Institute for the Study of War (ISW) warns that Putin is preparing to use this winter to break Kyiv, and will not enter serious negotiations if he believes he has a viable military path. Separately, Putin has ordered a probe following the humiliation of Russia's Navy Day parade. Russia has released former US Marine Robert Gilman, 32, after more than four years in prison; Putin granted a humanitarian pardon and Trump is credited with securing the release. The State Department stated explicitly that no prisoner exchange took place and Washington made no concessions. Fox News had framed the release as a prisoner exchange, which the US government has now denied. Gilman had been in a dissociative stupor for 47 days and was gravely ill; his father disputes the Russian account of his arrest. Trump has signed an executive order overhauling the childhood vaccine schedule, drawing pushback from doctors, pharma, and public health experts. A 7.4-magnitude earthquake — Colombia's strongest on record — has struck western Colombia, killing at least 240 people and leaving more than 3,000 missing; rescuers are racing to find survivors amid fears the death toll will rise steeply. A 32-year-old woman was pulled alive from a collapsed apartment on Tuesday, and footage circulating on social media shows a baby being rescued from the rubble of a destroyed building in Cali. The Trump administration has pledged $15.5 million in relief. Amid the earthquake aftermath, Colombia's new far-right President Abelardo de la Espriella, in office just over two weeks, has announced an immigration crackdown, ordering authorities to detain and deport migrants who are in the country irregularly or have committed crimes, echoing ally Donald Trump.

facts.state_of_play: Charges against ex-Olympian David Hearn and three other alleged vandals over the Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool were dismissed after prosecutors found damage was caused by a botched contractor installation. Trump is pushing DOJ to open a new case — specifically exploring a misdemeanor prosecution — a request made one day after Todd Blanche was sworn in to lead DOJ. A Trump-aligned advisor publicly warned Pirro she has more than the Reflecting Pool to worry about. House Judiciary Democrats under Raskin have launched a probe and sent letters to both the Justice and Interior Departments demanding records. Pirro and Burgum remain subjects of that probe. Separately, DOJ has arrested Heidi Beirich, former SPLC chief financial officer, in California on charges of conspiracy to commit wire fraud, conspiracy to submit false statements, and conspiracy to conceal money laundering, alleging she oversaw a $4.1 million scheme funneling donor funds to informants inside white supremacist groups. Beirich's lawyer characterizes the case as an attempt to silence political opponents. In an unrelated action, DOJ released a report finding that guards at two California state-run women's prisons routinely sexually abused inmates and that the corrections department failed to provide safe reporting channels. California has been given 49 days to remediate conditions or face civil litigation; state officials say reforms are already in place.

FIFA has also suspended Argentina's Leandro Paredes and other players, with fines and bans totaling 17 matches, over on-field clashes with Spain after the World Cup final. Separately, Argentina great Lionel Messi has announced his retirement from international football following Argentina's World Cup final defeat to Spain and the recent death of his father; he wrote his retirement letter after the final but delayed publishing it due to his father's health issues, revealed the decision via a social media post on Monday, and will continue playing club football for MLS side Inter Miami.

Vance describes the conflict as entering a 'new phase' centered on economic pressure. New US sanctions on Tehran are expected to be unveiled soon as Washington presses China and allies to join the campaign; Chinese analysts argue Beijing can resist by leveraging critical mineral supplies and its own oil reserves. The UAE, particularly Dubai, is seen as pivotal to the campaign's effectiveness. Iran's leadership, including President Masoud Pezeshkian, insists it is negotiating from a position of strength and claims the world acknowledges its victory, while other Iranian officials dismiss the economic threats as proof US military efforts have failed. Some reporting suggests US and global financial markets, rather than Iran, have been the first casualties of the escalating economic warfare. Separately, immigration authorities have detained family members of US military personnel, including the father of a USS Abraham Lincoln sailor, spotlighting a rising trend of ICE arrests targeting military families under the Trump administration.

facts.state_of_play: A massive Russian missile and drone barrage struck Kyiv overnight, killing 12-16 people and wounding around 40, hitting a children's hospital, a school, residential blocks and warehouses; Poland activated defensive measures in response, and officials cited Ukraine's ongoing air-defence interceptor shortages. Separately, Ukrainian strikes have knocked out nearly a third of Russia's major oil refineries, prompting fuel shortages and clashes at petrol stations, with Putin's government arresting Russians who complained. A new long-range drone strike set ablaze the Ust-Luga oil terminal near St Petersburg, prompting Putin to vow revenge and to intensify strikes on Ukraine's energy infrastructure ahead of winter, while also accusing Zelenskyy of terrorism. Kyiv has now been hit by Russian drones for a seventh consecutive day, and fresh attacks on Kyiv and Odesa regions wounded at least 8 more civilians. This is in addition to the earlier large-scale Ukrainian drone assault on Moscow region and the deadly Russian missile strike on a Kharkiv region village. Additionally, a Russian 'double-tap' drone strike hit a shopping mall in Kryvyi Rih, Zelensky's hometown, killing 15-16 people and injuring more than 100, with a second wave of drones striking as rescue workers responded. A day later, further Russian strikes killed 6 more Ukrainians, while a Ukrainian drone strike on a home in southern Russia killed two children and injured their parents. German Foreign Minister Johann Wadephul arrived in Kyiv by special train ahead of Ukraine's 35th independence day as Russia stepped up its attacks. The EU, Germany and France have now formally blamed Russia for a drone attack on Leipzig/Halle Airport, with Kaja Kallas calling it 'state-sponsored terrorism' and summoning Russia's envoy; UK Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband vowed Russia's attempts to divide Europe 'will fail.' Zelensky has urged airlines to avoid Russian airspace as Ukraine escalates its drone campaign and Russia vows to intensify strikes.

facts.state_of_play: Nigel Farage is under scrutiny after failing to declare a £5m gift from Thailand-based donor Christopher Harborne, and has dismissed the Commons Standards Committee probe as rigged, comparing his treatment to Donald Trump's and Boris Johnson's past cases, while pledging to strip MPs of power over standards punishments if he becomes PM, and now also threatens to overhaul the House of Lords and judiciary to deliver his 100-day plan. Separately, Reform UK has been reported to police over an undercover sting by Channel 4 News and investigative group Verbatim, alleging the party took payment from an American company for commissioned polling, breaching donation rules; police are reportedly in talks with the Electoral Commission. Farage was forced to suspend his closest aide Dan Jukes and head of policy James Orr, who is also a close friend of US Vice President JD Vance and known as his 'British Sherpa'; Cambridge University has launched its own probe into Orr. Farage dismissed the aides' recorded comments as 'loose pub talk' while conceding they 'don't look good', but has since told the BBC's Laura Kuenssberg he 'wasn't listening' to the donor talks and admitted his family are 'begging' him to quit politics amid 'very thoughtful moments' over his future, as splits emerge within the party and insiders reportedly call for a stronger operation. Farage now claims he knows donation law 'better than anybody' and predicts 'many more investigations' into Reform UK as he tries to salvage the final day of the party conference. Separately, a video showed Reform members pulling a heckler's hair during Farage's Birmingham conference speech, prompting condemnation from Zia Yusuf and a police appeal for the woman to come forward. Jordan Bardella addressed the conference and signed an Entente Cordiale agreement with Farage pledging to use the Royal Navy to intercept and return migrant boats to France. Reform also unveiled a 100-day plan to halt small boat crossings, cut taxes—including raising the tax-free personal allowance to £15,000—and scrap green levies to save households £250, as home affairs spokesman Zia Yusuf's call to use the Royal Marines to 'arrest' migrants fuelled speculation about a bid to succeed Farage.

facts.state_of_play: Andy Burnham, now Prime Minister, faces scrutiny over an undeclared £6,600 Japan party from his time as Manchester Mayor. On his first foreign trip as PM, he traveled to Kyiv for Ukraine's 35th independence day, co-chairing a coalition-of-the-willing meeting, meeting Zelenskyy, playing guitar with Ukrainian soldiers, and announcing UK sharing of classified Storm Shadow missile-component technology and long-range missile blueprints, including support for France in setting up missile assembly lines, to boost Ukraine's missile production. Ukraine has reciprocated with a trove of secret intelligence data to help the UK train troops using AI as part of a landmark military agreement. Burnham has directly challenged Putin over the war's origins, asking 'Who started the fire?', amid Kremlin warnings that the UK is now 'participating in this war,' with a senior Putin adviser threatening a 'semi-military' response and possible attacks on UK drone factories, calling Britain 'evil number one' and declaring that 'Pandora's box has been opened.' Backbenchers have warned Burnham against calling a snap general election. Burnham says he is likely to travel to New York next month for the UN General Assembly, where he plans to meet Donald Trump and lobby, alongside other European leaders, for the US to supply Ukraine with Patriot missiles, calling the current supply problem 'fixable.' He has also said Prince Harry and Meghan's security arrangements are a private matter. Meanwhile, Zelenskyy says Russia plans to draft 300,000 more troops amid reports of increasingly aggressive and intimidating recruitment tactics as Russia prepares for a winter offensive, has warned on the prospect of wartime elections, and declared in a defiant independence day speech that Ukraine wants peace but will not give in to Russia at any price, as Ukrainian drones struck three major Russian retail hubs near Moscow, with Ozon identified as the next targeted economic pressure point, and attempted to strike a military cosmodrome; Ukraine marked the day with a parade featuring robots replacing soldiers. Moscow has since struck a cargo ship in the Black Sea after Zelenskyy called for talks to halt attacks, with Kyiv vowing to bolster regional air defences amid a renewed Black Sea blockade squeezing Ukraine's grain exports and farmers. Separately, the first British national is reported to have been killed fighting for Russia in a drone attack, and Burnham has signalled openness to cut-price tuition fees for EU students as part of a planned EU 'reset' summit. A key Ukraine ally was notably absent from the Kyiv gathering. Trump has dispatched envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner to Moscow and Kyiv this weekend bearing a fresh US peace plan to end the war, their first visit to Kyiv since Trump's return to office; Moscow is reported to have violated a Zelenskyy-proposed air truce, a drone struck a Ukrainian intelligence (SBU) facility in Kyiv, and Trump said he does not believe Russia intends to attack NATO. The envoys' planned Kremlin meeting with Putin has now taken place, with Putin telling them the situation in Ukraine remains 'difficult,' and both Russia and Ukraine have vowed not to strike each other's capitals for three days during the talks. Russia insisted the US must 'consider realities on the ground,' and Trump said there may be a good chance for a deal. Separately, former MI6 chief John Sawers said enduring peace is unlikely while Putin remains in office and that talks could begin next year.

Iran has responded by attacking US bases in the Middle East, and reports indicate the US also struck Iranian tankers. This escalation comes as Iran and Oman continue negotiating a temporary reopening of the Strait of Hormuz, including a revenue-sharing arrangement, a temporary shipping lane and mine clearing, with disagreements persisting over navigation, jurisdiction and costs. Iran says military vessels would be banned from transiting under the deal and is demanding the US lift its blockade before finalizing the agreement. Trump has publicly disputed any blockade, calling the strait 'functioning' and claiming the US Navy fully cleared Iranian mines, but US allies privately warn the strait may still be mined; Trump says he is in no hurry for Iran to resume talks. Meanwhile, the USS Abraham Lincoln, whose deployment was extended due to the US war in Iran, is nearing the end of its mission after 270-plus days at sea and is preparing to dock thousands of sailors and marines in Pattaya, Thailand, prompting heightened security measures and warnings about local prostitution laws.

Iran's president said further fighting with the US was not in Iran's interest, while the Strait of Hormuz remains closed by Iran amid a US naval counter-blockade. Trump shared AI-generated footage claiming Iran's Kharg Island was destroyed, forcing a Pentagon denial; VP JD Vance later said the post was a deliberate message to Iran, while Trump has also mused about the US taking over the island, which holds ~90% of Iran's oil exports. Oil prices rose above $90/barrel on supply concerns, while US stocks fell (S&P 500 -0.3%) amid the renewed conflict. Iran's foreign minister accused Netanyahu of tricking the US into war, and the conflict enters its seventh month. UK think-tanks estimate the war will cost British households £2,400 each. The UAE said it intercepted an Iranian drone over its waters, and the EU pledged at the G20 to maintain economic pressure on Iran alongside the US. Separately, Russia has reportedly been secretly supplying Iran with supersonic cruise missile technology, marking a significant deepening of Russia-Iran military cooperation. This follows earlier US cancellation of a joint marine exercise with South Korea and new Treasury sanctions targeting Iran-linked banks.

Palestinian American homeowner Louai (Loui) Abo Ridi, back from Ohio after 10 days under siege, has directly confronted settlers outside his home despite Israeli military deployment, demanding protection from Israeli forces and the U.S. government. A new Yesh Din report finds settler attacks in Palestinian-administered West Bank areas have almost doubled since 2025 amid a self-proclaimed 'great settlement revolution,' with AJLabs analysis putting the rate at six attacks a day. Separately, settler children attacked a Red Crescent ambulance, the Board of Peace reversed course on a Gaza disarmament deal, Christian families report growing pressure to leave, and Israel opened tenders for over 1,200 homes in the E1 settlement, prompting France, Germany, Britain and Italy to join Europe and Canada in condemning the plan as making Palestinian statehood impossible. An Israeli minister also faces backlash over a gallows site with a 'viewing booth' for hanging Palestinians.

Melania Trump attended alongside aide Natalie Harp and son Eric Trump, marking Melania's second public appearance this week. A scary crash occurred on Lap 36 when David Malukas clipped the inside wall and Sting Ray Robb T-boned his stopped car. Nolan Siegel, Marcus Ericsson, and Mick Schumacher had faced six-place grid penalties for engine changes. The event drew large crowds along a route past the Capitol Building and down Pennsylvania Avenue, with drivers reaching speeds up to 185 mph, though attendees faced logistical chaos including long water lines amid sweltering heat. The White House also faced online accusations of plagiarizing promotional graphics, allegedly resembling Rolex 24 race materials.
